accepted_edits.reason: all three s61/s62 findings were answered acted and v315 applies exactly those edits, plus the review-index attribution and /dev/shm record reckon-a6 supplied for the census

findings.reason: a node reading "decoded" literally fails its own head arm on the first attempt; the repair is to name the instrument and the warm state (one call to build the index, the cache cleared, the test's own call counted), which is a change to this sentence.
findings.text: s61's head arm asserts "at most 60" row records decoded on a temporary ledger. The count's instrument is unstated and the two readings part company by the whole ledger: a count of rows returned by the read holds at 30 under a window bound, but a count of payload records decoded from the source holds at 2,030 on the first call, because `ledger.load` on a ledger with no index "still reads every source to build it" (reckon/ledger.py:2260-2261) and `_load_aggregate` parses the aggregate envelope whole (reckon/ledger.py:989-1000). The base control of 2,030 is equally consistent with either reading, so the head's 60 is unsatisfiable on a cold read and satisfiable on a warm one, and the plan does not say which state the measurement is taken in

findings.reason: without an expected relation between the cleared and uncleared runs the control cannot fail, so the census's attribution would rest on a well-formed log rather than on a measure, and the node must invent the relation itself.
findings.text: s62's negative control is a recording, not a control, and it encodes the conclusion the section exists to test. It reads "the same harness run for 2 ticks with every reckon in-process memo cleared between ticks records the retained total that the growing sites account for": it states no expected value and no comparison against the uncleared run, so whatever the harness writes satisfies it; and "every reckon in-process memo" is not an enumerable instrument, since memos are per-module caches and dicts with no common clear — precisely what the census has not yet established — so if the retained memory is held by a structure that is not a memo, the cleared run looks identical to an instrument that cannot see growth at all

findings.reason: at 79 live pointers the node's only options are to report blocked or to deviate from the write guard, and either is a round trip the plan could have priced in with a temporary-root population, or a floor read from the store at run time.
findings.text: s62's integer floor "at least 80 live pointers" is drawn from the live crew home that the same done-when requires not be written to, so the artifact's population is set by fleet state the node cannot control. The store holds 139 pointer files as this review reads it, which leaves headroom today, but on a quiet fleet the node has neither a fallback population nor an instruction, and writing 80 synthetic pointers is forbidden by the same sentence's mtime guard

response_events.note: s61 now names the instrument and state: the test first builds the ledger's on-disk index (the live ledger has one), then counts payload records decoded from row sources by one _lane_reference_rates call for a new bucket: at most 60 at head, 2,030 at base

s62's control is now a positive control: the harness injects a test-only module-level list growing by 50 MB per tick, and the census must attribute at least 45 MB per tick of retained growth to that site; a census that cannot see it fails
s62 now runs over the live pointers present when the job runs and records that count; it states the count and runs the 6 ticks whatever it is, with no floor tied to fleet state
